ing: very fresh, cut into 0.5 inch cubes
st: Buy tuna labeled safe to eat raw and keep it cold. Cut it into small even cubes about 0.5 inch wide.
Put the tuna in a glass or ceramic bowl and pour over the lime juice. Stir to coat all pieces.
Refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes until the outside of the fish turns pale and firm.
Stir the coconut milk, red onion, chili, green onion, salt and pepper in another bowl.
Drain off most of the lime juice from the tuna.
Pour the coconut mixture over the tuna and gently fold to combine.
Chill for another 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Taste, add salt or lime if needed, then sprinkle with cilantro and serve cold with rice or breadfruit.

ing: such as snapper or mahi-mahi, 4 pieces
st: Pat the fish dry and rub with the juice of one lime, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Rest 10 minutes.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, beaten eggs, and the coconut.
Dip a fillet in the flour and shake off the extra.
Dip it in the egg, letting the extra drip off.
Press it firmly into the coconut so it is covered all over.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until a shred of coconut sizzles.
Fry the fillets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the coconut is golden and the fish flakes (145°F/63°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve right away with lime wedges.
Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water in a small bowl and let it soak for 5 minutes.
Heat the coconut milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Whisk the egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until pale.
Slowly whisk the hot coconut milk into the yolks, then pour everything back into the pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 5 to 7 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon (170°F/77°C) so the eggs are cooked.
Remove from the heat and stir in the soaked gelatin and vanilla until dissolved. Cool to room temperature.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold the whipped cream into the cooled coconut custard.
Spoon into glasses and chill for at least 4 hours until set.
Top with toasted coconut and serve cold.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9 inch round cake pan or loaf pan.
Mix the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix in the mashed bananas.
Add the flour mixture in two parts, alternating with the milk, until just combined.
Fold in [[0.75 cup]] coconut.
Pour into the pan and sprinkle the rest of the coconut on top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean and the top is golden.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then turn out and cool before slicing.
